result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=with, B=without): Both answers turn down the hero stat and the bigger cards for the right reason: they would use up the rows needed to show every truck. Both suggest a slim count strip, multi-column compact rows and per-status time thresholds that flag exceptions. B wins narrowly because it explains status encoding more fully (chip text plus an edge bar, not color alone), keeps rows stable by sorting by door within each status, ties the flagged rows directly to what the user wanted from bigger cards, and asks useful questions about yard layout and screen type. A adds a useful cap that flagged rows stay near 10%, but its diagram is misaligned and its six columns are cramped at half-width. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): Both answers reject the hero stat and large cards for the right reason, keep all trucks visible in multi-column compact rows, and use a slim count strip in place of a hero. B is slightly stronger on scannability: it right-aligns tabular minutes so they scan as a column, sets out a clear visual hierarchy within each row, encodes status as a dot plus the word, and caps exceptions at about 10% of rows. A is just as sound on keeping rows quiet and stable, but it says less about alignment and how status colors are used.
